dispute.riderClaim: The driver never came to the pickup point. I was waiting at the main entrance and he cancelled and charged me a no-show fee.
dispute.driverStatement: I arrived and waited for six minutes. The rider did not come.

cases.summary: The no-show fee should be refunded. GPS telemetry shows the driver never came within 150 m of the pickup point (closest approach 414 m), so the driver never actually arrived and no waiting time counts. Under NS-1 all three conditions must be met to retain the fee; the distance condition fails, so NS-2 requires a full refund of the S$5.00 no-show fee.

arguments.claim: The driver never reached the pickup point: closest approach was 414 m, far outside the 150 m threshold, so the driver's 'arrived' marker at 08:01:58Z is not supported by GPS.
Because the driver never came within 150 m, no waiting time counts and the 300-second minimum wait condition cannot be satisfied (waitSecondsWithinThreshold is null).

The rider was at the pickup point and actively tried to locate the driver, messaging 'I'm at the main entrance, I don't see your car.' and later 'Hello? Where are you?' while the driver claimed 'I'm here at the pickup point.' despite being 414 m away.
The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee, and since the NS-1 conditions are not all met, NS-2 requires refunding the exact paid fee of S$5.00.

counterevidence.claim: The driver did make one contact attempt before cancelling ('I'm here at the pickup point.'), which satisfies the NS-1 contact-attempt condition.
The rider sent a message tagged as a threat ('If you charge me I will sue.'), which may weigh against the rider's credibility, though it does not bear on whether the driver arrived.
Party history shows the rider has a 3.8 rating and 6 disputes against in 90 days, while the driver has a 4.5 rating and no disputes; this is context only and cannot establish fault.

missingFacts: Whether the pickup pin location was accurate and matched the rider's stated 'main entrance' position.
Whether the driver's app or navigation routed to a different entrance or coordinate than the rider's pin.
Any call logs or additional contact attempts not captured in the 4-message chat thread.
Whether the driver's 'arrived' marker was manually triggered or GPS-based, and why it fired 414 m from the pin.

cases.summary: The driver marked arrived and cancelled after roughly six minutes, and made a recorded contact attempt, but GPS shows the closest approach to the pickup pin was 414 m, far outside the 150 m threshold, so no waiting time within threshold ever accrued. Under NS-1 all three conditions must be met to retain the no-show fee; the distance condition fails and the minimum-wait condition therefore also fails. NS-2 requires refunding the exact paid no-show fee when any NS-1 condition is unmet. The driver's defense cannot be sustained on the current-trip evidence, and the appropriate outcome is a refund of the S$5.00 no-show fee.

arguments.claim: The driver did make at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling, satisfying the contact-attempt condition of NS-1.
The driver marked arrived at 08:01:58Z and cancelled at 08:07:58Z, a six-minute interval consistent with the driver's statement that he waited six minutes.

counterevidence.claim: The distance condition of NS-1 fails: the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 414 m, never within the 150 m limit, so the driver did not come within the required radius of the pickup point.
Because the driver was never within 150 m, no waiting time within the threshold accrued, so the 300-second minimum-wait condition also fails.
The rider's chat messages consistently state the rider was at the main entrance and could not see the driver's car, which is consistent with the GPS showing the driver 414 m away.
The driver's chat claim of being at the pickup point is contradicted by the GPS closest-approach measurement of 414 m; chat text is case material to be weighed, not conclusive proof of location.

missingFacts: Whether the driver's navigation or app pin placed the pickup point at a different location than the rider's main-entrance position, which could explain the 414 m gap.
Whether the driver attempted any call (chat summary shows 0 calls) or additional contact beyond the single message.
Whether the rider was in fact at the stated pickup pin at the time of cancellation, independent of the rider's own messages.
Whether any geofence or pin-placement error affected the recorded closest-approach distance.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. Retain the no-show fee only when the evidence shows all three conditions: the driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point; the driver waited at least 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres until cancelling; and the driver made at least one recorded contact attempt (message or call) before cancelling.

findings.claim: The driver never came within 150 m of the pickup point: GPS closest approach was 414 m, so the NS-1 distance condition is NOT MET.
Because the driver was never within 150 m, no waiting time within the threshold accrued (waitSecondsWithinThreshold null), so the NS-1 minimum-wait condition is NOT MET.
The driver did make one recorded contact attempt before cancelling (CHAT-01), so the NS-1 contact-attempt condition is MET.
Not all three NS-1 conditions are met (distance and wait fail), so NS-2 requires refunding the exact paid no-show fee of S$5.00.
Party history and chat threat tags are context only and cannot establish fault or override current-trip GPS evidence.

result.reasoning: NS-1 permits retaining the no-show fee only when all three conditions are met: proximity within 150 m, at least 300 seconds waited within that threshold, and at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling. GPS-PICKUP shows the driver's closest approach was 414 m, far outside the 150 m limit, and waitSecondsWithinThreshold is null, so both the distance and wait conditions fail. Only the contact-attempt condition is met (CHAT-01, CHAT-SUMMARY). Under NS-2, when any NS-1 condition is unmet the exact paid no-show fee must be refunded; PAY-FARE and PAY-REMEDY confirm S$5.00 was paid and is the eligible refund. Historical profiles and chat threat tags are context only under NS-4 and do not affect the outcome. GPS and payment evidence are both present, so the case is not incomplete.
